acceptance: Live scoped credential and transport proof shows fork writer stays in fork, core has no fork-write token, core App has only intended contents/PR rights, and authorized machine identity is recorded without exposing credentials.
Canonical producer delivery replay proves fork verification at merged SHA; core replay proves only origin/identity/hash, transactional adoption, core wrapper/SQL and installed wheel/sdist behavior.

Fork and core production dry-runs make no hosted mutations, both kill switches are exercised, and cutover leaves exactly one upstream controller with old core producer disabled only after replacement proof.
Actual App-created core PR and App-armed merge trigger ordinary core PR and trunk CI; normal fork/core protection and generic reviews remain enforced without Theseus changes.

Required core Q19 reliability work and all capabilities/docs merged; enable only after evidence and live readback. If an owner-only step is missing, remain blocked with exact next action, never call the workflow activated.

After replacement proof, an ordinary core cleanup PR removes legacy producer workflow/script/dedicated tests plus obsolete mandatory fork-diff tooling/references; fork diagnostic replacement is documented before removal.
Credential owner removes the obsolete core SQLGLOT_FORK_REFRESH_TOKEN after cutover; no fork-write credential remains in core, and existing freshness/advisory release gates are retained unchanged.
context: Owner instruction 2026-11-05 supersedes BOTH rejected designs. benchbox-sqlglot owns upstream discovery/integration, fork PR lifecycle, source/relocation/runtime/engine/distribution validation and trustworthy wheel delivery. BenchBox core owns consuming that delivery, origin/identity/hash binding, transactional pin updates, its own wrapper/benchmark-definition/installed-package concerns and ordinary core PR landing. Core must not discover upstream, merge fork PRs, reconstruct/re-review fork source, repeat fork test matrices or acquire a fork-write credential. Theseus stays unchanged and generic; no special policy, external-source inlet, synthetic dataset, second model-review path or reviewer release is needed. Theseus PR25 closed unmerged; prior approval claims withdrawn. This supersedes the source-review-at-core portion of sqlglot-fork-review-h1-governance, not existing protected-branch rules or ordinary review requirements. Preserve exact merged-SHA producer evidence, scoped independent credentials, no candidate execution with write/reviewer secrets, no golden/outcome/test/waiver changes, reviewed rollback, human holds/disarms, reverted-delivery suppression and no public release/cloud spend. Update current fork/core runbooks to this boundary. Corrected proposal: local://sqlglot-end-to-end-proposal.md. The live tracker, not discarded branch code or prior notes, owns delivery state.
description:
Prove deployed fork producer and core consumer independently, then perform safe cutover. Fork needs its own scoped PR/contents writer that starts required CI; core must never receive it. SQLGLOT_FORK_REFRESH_TOKEN was configured in core for the legacy producer: credential owner configures an appropriate writer in fork, since GitHub cannot return its secret value for copying. Prove read-only artifact transport separately and core-scoped contents/PR App mutation without statuses/checks/workflow write. Verify configured authorized machine identity and actual PR/trunk event triggering; use the App for core arming. Do not install new reviewer credentials or modify Theseus.

Exercise actual canonical verified artifact delivery in fork and core-only adoption/install binding in a disposable lower-version checkout. Use #80 or the newest unexpired canonical delivery, never an unbound rebuild. Run both deployed no-write dry-runs, test separate kill switches, prove replacement fork producer before disabling legacy core upstream producer and confirm one active upstream writer. Q19 remains a consumer activation reliability prerequisite only, not a fork implementation gate. Preserve public-release/security constraints. No-op proves deployment, not a real successful release; keep empirical certification separate. Missing owner-only secret/identity/access remains an exact blocked action, not a Theseus release prerequisite.

Cutover explicitly includes a narrow CORE removal PR after live fork replacement proof: remove scripts/sqlglot_fork_refresh.py, .github/workflows/sqlglot-fork-refresh.yml and their dedicated tests/callers; retire the mandatory core PR-template fork-diff checkbox and make sqlglot-fork-diff script/target/test references in favor of documented fork-owned git diff/producer diagnostics and delivery evidence. This is activation-owned core decommissioning, not a fork-controller cross-repo edit or a prerequisite of the core-consumer implementation. The docs replacement is already a dependency, avoiding any cycle. After producer cutover and ordinary reviewed core removal merge, credential owner deletes the obsolete core SQLGLOT_FORK_REFRESH_TOKEN secret. Do not delete that secret before the producer is working or remove unrelated issues/branches. Retain scripts/check_sqlglot_upstream_freshness.py and scripts/check_sqlglot_advisories.py release policy unchanged; moving these gates needs a separate owner decision.
